title: Lending & Flash-Funding Arbitrage — Practitioner Testimony Operator Workbook
subtitle: Practitioner worksheets for structuring double closes, pricing transactional funding, controlling title and escrow, protecting earnest money, and moving clean wires from contract to settlement

worksheets.title: Double Close or Assign: Structure, Closer and Funding Map
worksheets.purpose: Decide whether this deal exits by assignment or a two-contract double close, lock a closer who handles back-to-back escrows, secure the end buyer's deposit, and price both legs in dollars before any money moves on the A-to-B purchase.
instructions: Start with the spread and the contract paper; a no-assignment clause or a deed restriction decides the structure before personal preference does.
Tell the closing agent the exact structure you want before sending contracts, and ask your transactional funder first if unsure.
Convert every funding quote into dollars on this purchase price, and price the double close as two full closings.
Lock the end buyer's non-refundable deposit and the release clause at contract execution, not on closing day.
Do not authorize any A-leg funding until the end buyer's B-to-C money is confirmed sitting in escrow.

fields.name: spread_and_exit_trigger
fields.prompt: Write the contracted purchase price, the expected resale price, and the resulting spread on this deal. Then state the exact dollar threshold you use to switch from an assignment to a double close, and name the practitioner benchmark you are measuring against.
fields.example: Contract at $100,000, resale at $120,000, spread $20,000. Under Jamil Damji's house rule this stays an assignment, because Key Glee only double closes when profit runs above $20,000, a trigger raised from $15,000 after sellers rarely objected [Jamil Damji — KMD0dZIIYwc @ 00:02:12]. Brent Daniels sets his line at $15,000 and Lex Levinrad at $10,000.

fields.name: no_assignment_screen
fields.prompt: Identify whether the seller paper allows assignment at all. Note if the property is REO, HUD, bank-owned, hedge-fund, auction, or short sale inventory, and check for deed restrictions that bar resale for a set number of days or above a percentage.
fields.example: Bank-owned house with a no-assignment clause, so assignment is off the table and the plan becomes two contracts and two closings. Before promising the end buyer a same-day double close, the deed is screened for a restriction barring resale for 30, 60 or 90 days or above a set percentage [Game Changer Real Estate Insights — lLbfcHAX30o @ 00:03:38].

fields.name: closer_selection
fields.prompt: Name the title company or closing attorney who will handle both legs. Record whether they confirmed in writing that they handle double escrows, how you found them, and the exact closing-services clause you will write into both contracts.
fields.example: Closer sourced by posting in a local fix-and-flip group asking which escrow officers actually run double escrows [Brent Daniels - Wholesaling Inc — 1CnG4yCPR4M @ 00:03:10]. Both contracts carry the line 'seller or buyer agrees to use the closing services of' followed by that investor-friendly title company, because the wrong title company will kill the deal [Flipping Mastery TV — Jfl-5LgDTaM @ 00:09:55].

fields.name: structure_briefing
fields.prompt: Describe the exact closing structure you will tell the closing agent before any contract is sent. Spell out who funds the A-to-B leg, whether the end buyer's wire may fund both sides, and the wording you will avoid with a nervous closer.
fields.example: Agent told up front: two independent back-to-back closings, leg one funded by outside transactional cash, because an ABC closing means different things to different agents [LearnREInvesting — _QXnSUQsTNw @ 00:04:14]. The phrase 'ABC closing' is never used with a nervous closer; when one attorney firm refused, moving the file to a high-volume investor attorney closed both legs cleanly.

fields.name: funding_camp
fields.prompt: State which camp your deal falls into: leg one closes with outside cash, or the end buyer's wire funds both legs. Explain why, and record whether your title company allows the buyer's money to pay for your own purchase.
fields.example: Outside cash camp. Kevin Tacher and the funders insist leg one closes with independent money, matching the rule that all deals must be closed independent of each other, which means closing A must close cash [Game Changer Real Estate Insights — lLbfcHAX30o @ 00:01:46]. Title was asked early, since some will not let the buyer's money pay for the wholesaler's purchase.

fields.name: buyer_deposit_lock
fields.prompt: Record the non-refundable deposit amount your cash buyer posts at contract execution, where it is held, and the exact release clause that lets escrow pay it to you without any further escrow instruction if the buyer fails to close.
fields.example: End buyer posts $5,000 non-refundable at title on signing, above Jerry Norton's $2,500 floor and inside his preferred $5,000 to $10,000 band [Flipping Mastery TV — Jfl-5LgDTaM @ 00:11:13]. The release clause needs no further escrow instruction, so a buyer who flakes on closing day forfeits directly to the wholesaler and the deposit covers the wholesaler's exposure.

fields.name: funder_quote_comparison
fields.prompt: List each transactional funder you contacted, their pricing model, any upfront fee, and when they will wire. Convert every quote into a dollar figure on this purchase price so you compare actual costs rather than percentages or flat headlines.
fields.example: On a $100,000 purchase, Bright Closings at 1% plus $100 processing costs $1,100, paid from the second closing [Jasper Cool — EUE6UWl2qBA @ 00:03:19]. Flip Lab Capital quotes 1% to 3% plus the wholesaler's closing costs. Velocity Capital charges a $250 initiation fee at submission, subtracted from the back-end fee when the deal closes [Closer Control — qtTEzFSMqJg @ 00:14:38].

fields.name: two_closing_budget
fields.prompt: Itemize the full cost of running this deal as two complete closings: both sets of title work, title insurance on each leg, recording fees, transfer taxes on each deed, the funding fee, and the break you will ask title to give.
fields.example: David Olds ran a $100,000 contract resold at $120,000 both ways: $20,000 on assignment versus $14,000 net on a double close, roughly $6,000 to $7,000 lost to title [David Olds REI — oXZTulq2Qx0 @ 00:02:13]. B-to-C costs stay on the end buyer as if it were an assignment, and title is asked for an A-to-B discount since they earn double in an hour.

fields.name: spread_protection
fields.prompt: Explain how you will keep the seller from seeing the resale price and the end buyer from seeing your buy price. Note where your business name and profit will appear on the settlement statement and who will review it line by line.
fields.example: Double close chosen because the spread is large and the seller is squirmy. One operator took a speaker phone call from an attorney and a seller who went line by line through the HUD and found the business name beside $30,000 [Closer Control — qtTEzFSMqJg @ 00:09:34]. Buyers and sellers have walked when a wholesale fee looked too high.

fields.name: funding_release_and_slippage
fields.prompt: Write the funding release condition and the slippage plan. Confirm the end buyer's funds must sit in escrow before the A leg moves, how the funder will wire, and what extra fees or interest apply if the second closing is delayed.
fields.example: No money moves on the A leg until B-to-C funds land in escrow, since promised same-day funding is worth nothing until it arrives [Ryan Schrope — j30R1Cef6PE @ 00:18:13]. Wire instructions were locked on the first call. Slippage is budgeted: a $150,000 borrow runs about $3,000 plus roughly $50 a day in interest [The Virtual Investor — kCbwtS3VKw4 @ 00:07:16].

worksheets.completion_gate: Gate passed only when the B-to-C contract is signed, the end buyer's non-refundable deposit of at least $2,500 is posted with a release clause, the closer has confirmed in writing that they run double escrows, and the end buyer's funds are confirmed in escrow before the A leg is funded.

worksheets.title: Transactional Funding Costs and Title Control
worksheets.purpose: Select a transactional lender on net dollar cost and execution, model the real net profit after two sets of closing costs, and take control of title, the settlement statement, signing logistics and wire verification from contract to recording.
instructions: Get every funder quote in writing on the actual A-to-B amount, with all wire, processing, rush, hold and split title fees listed.
Walk away from any funder demanding a large upfront application fee or pushing a 24-hour funding deadline.
Open escrow and pull title the day the contract is signed rather than waiting for a cash buyer.
Ask for the reissue credit and challenge the lien search charge; title discounts neither unless asked.
Verify wire instructions by calling escrow a second time and send a true wire, never ACH.

fields.name: net_dollar_fee_comparison
fields.prompt: Convert each funder's advertised percentage into net dollars on your actual A-to-B amount. Record the minimum fee, which funding figure the percentage applies to, and whether any quote crosses the 1% line practitioners treat as overpaying on a standard deal.
fields.example: On a $200,000 double closing, 3/4 of 1% costs $1,500 while 2% costs $4,000; a half point equals $1,000 and a full point equals $2,000 [LearnREInvesting — 0u7L7Q7CE5o @ 00:01:11]. Dave Dinkel says no one should pay more than 1% of the A-to-B funds unless the lender negotiates below its quote or the amount exceeds one million dollars.

fields.name: junk_fee_audit
fields.prompt: List every charge beyond the core funding fee: application, entry, processing, cancellation, wire, document rush, extended hold, and split title company fees. Get the total expected funding charge in writing and flag any minimum that dominates a small deal.
fields.example: Written quote requested covering wire, processing, document rush, extended hold and split title company fees [LearnREInvesting — 0u7L7Q7CE5o @ 00:02:30]. Minimums run as high as $1,795, which swamps a small A-to-B purchase. Some lenders charge an application fee just to decide whether they will fund, though LearnREInvesting says transactional funding should carry no upfront cost [LearnREInvesting — l-l8leRQ_KE @ 00:00:00].

fields.name: funder_red_flags
fields.prompt: Screen each funder for walk-away signals before you submit the deal. Record any large upfront application fee, any pressured 24-hour funding deadline, and whether your title company has actually heard of the funder and closed with them before.
fields.example: One funder pushed a 24-hour deadline and a large application fee, both walk-away signals [The Full Deal REI — H-3pmQVYvCI @ 00:06:51], and title had never heard of it. The cleaner model funds on closing day once everybody has signed, sending money directly to the closing company to close the seller contract, then the end buyer contract [Velocity Advantage Capital — Fb1_zsDd4XE @ 00:01:26].

fields.name: lender_execution_vs_price
fields.prompt: Decide whether price or execution drives your lender choice on this deal. Record the funder's track record, how they handle roadblocks, whether they skip credit checks and underwriting, and why you would or would not pay more for experience.
fields.example: Execution wins here. A single percentage printed on a website is not the deciding factor; an experienced provider who helps when roadblocks hit is [LearnREInvesting — 0u7L7Q7CE5o @ 00:03:07]. Veteran Innovative Lending cites 424 deals closed and $21.1 million funded in 2025, with no credit checks, no income verification and no underwriting [Fund My Real Estate Deal — a--96aHg5xs @ 00:01:59].

fields.name: net_profit_model
fields.prompt: Build a net profit model for this double close. Enter the A-to-B price, B-to-C price, funded amount including closing costs, funding fee, wire fee, and both sets of closing costs, then confirm the spread absorbs everything.
fields.example: Tennessee deal: $38,000 A-to-B purchase resold for $72,900. Transactional funding of $39,727.93 covered the buy at 1% plus a $50 wire fee, the investor posted no earnest money, and net profit came to $30,070.71 [LearnREInvesting — BbugvWp8qsA @ 00:00:42]. If the spread cannot absorb the fee plus two sets of closing costs, it is not a double close deal.

fields.name: title_company_lock
fields.prompt: Name the wholesaler-friendly title company or closing attorney, the date escrow opened, and when title first called the seller. Note whether that closer is locked into the seller contract and whose legal department supplied your closing documents.
fields.example: Escrow opened the day the contract was signed, because about 25% of deals never reach closing over title issues [Flipping Mastery TV — 3aAzZildhKk @ 00:04:22]. The buyer's title of choice is locked into the seller contract. The company's staff attorney, reached through the legal department, supplied free assignment and double-close documents the company is comfortable closing [Jamil Damji — _4J_JXkaaMg @ 00:10:26].

fields.name: title_fee_hygiene
fields.prompt: Audit the title fee schedule line by line. Record the lien search charge, any padded junk charges, which fees are set by state rate filings versus unregulated, and whether you requested the reissue credit on the second-side policy.
fields.example: Lien search billed at $250 against an actual title company cost of $50 to $100, so it was negotiated down and the written report kept in the file [Flip With Rick — itXS_PDnxa8 @ 00:11:40]. The reissue credit was requested on the second-side policy, cutting a $2,000 premium by at least $1,000, since title will not offer it unless asked.

fields.name: settlement_statement_type
fields.prompt: Identify which settlement statement each party will receive: ALTA, HUD-1, or Closing Disclosure. Then decide how the assignment fee or spread will appear: exposed on the buyer's statement, hidden through a blind HUD, or separated by a double close.
fields.example: Cash investment purchase, so the closer issues a HUD rather than a lender CD paired with an ALTA [Tony Zowd — KmNl8nlbUxw @ 00:01:17]. On assignments, the escrow officer can run a blind HUD [Jamil Damji — _4J_JXkaaMg @ 00:06:51]. In one deal the listing agent placed the student's profit on page two, so the seller saw nothing on page one.

fields.name: signing_logistics
fields.prompt: Map the signing day: when the seller signs notarized documents, when the buyer signs, whether the two parties will ever share the office, and how a slow mortgage payoff or other lien will be cleared without stalling the file.
fields.example: Seller signs notarized documents before the slow mortgage payoff arrives, so the file can move to close the moment the payoff lands [Flipping Mastery TV — 0A2TpKfV1Os @ 00:10:20]. The buyer signs only the buyer side on a separate visit, because Jerry Norton virtually never lets buyers and sellers run into each other at the office [Flipping Mastery TV — 0A2TpKfV1Os @ 00:08:41].

fields.name: wire_verification_and_recording
fields.prompt: Document your wire controls and final step. Record the number you called to verify instructions a second time, confirm the transfer is a true wire and not ACH, and note when the deed records relative to keys changing hands.
fields.example: Before sending the actual wire, the escrow company was called one more time to verify the information directly [Tom Olsewski - Team Olsewski — haXXzqITogY @ 00:01:08]. A true wire went out, never ACH, and never cash, since title companies do not accept or keep cash [Realtypath — XlKk96ekJTE @ 01:03:08]. Keys transfer only after the deed has recorded, never before.

worksheets.completion_gate: Gate passed only when the written all-in funding charge fits inside the spread with two sets of closing costs, escrow is open with the chosen title company locked into the seller contract, the settlement statement format is confirmed, and wire instructions have been verified by a second call.

worksheets.title: Earnest Money, Proof of Funds and Clean Wires
worksheets.purpose: Protect the earnest money deposit through live written contingencies and calendared deadlines, present proof of funds that matches the offer, recalculate prorations that change cash due, and harden every wire against interception before settlement.
instructions: Calendar every contractual deadline at ratification and assign one person to read them aloud daily.
Cancel in writing by day nine or ten of a 10-day inspection period when the seller refuses credits or a price cut.
Match the name, amount and address on the proof of funds exactly to the offer.
Highlight every closing statement line that cannot be explained in one sentence and get who, what period and what document before signing.
Wire only on instructions that came directly from title, confirmed by calling title yourself on a number established early.

fields.name: emd_amount_and_holder
fields.prompt: Record the earnest money amount, the percentage of price it represents, and the neutral holder: title, brokerage trust account, or attorney escrow. Note the form of payment allowed and how the deposit will credit at closing.
fields.example: $19,500 on a $650,000 offer, the 3% scripted benchmark, held in escrow and applied to down payment or closing costs [Beyond the Address — 1ysRoNF77u8 @ 00:00:29]. Payment goes by wire or cashier's check only, since cash, debit and credit cards are not accepted [Kristie Dimarakis — NwZ7Oa8GUXQ @ 00:02:01]. Contract reads 'check or wire' in the earnest money delivery field.

fields.name: contingency_exits
fields.prompt: List every live written contingency protecting the deposit: inspection, loan, appraisal, and title. For each, record the deadline date, the exact cancellation method, and the real defects that would justify using it instead of cosmetic complaints.
fields.example: Inspection contingency reserved for water heater straps, HVAC, plumbing and electrical, with paint and carpet left at the door, so a seller refusal on real defects is a clean exit with the deposit [Andrew Finney Team — ND7J57hzroE @ 00:02:01]. The loan contingency stays in, even in a multiple-bid fight, because without it the buyer is on the hook.

fields.name: deadline_calendar
fields.prompt: Calendar every contractual deadline on the day the contract is ratified. Record the inspection period length, the date you must cancel in writing, who reads the deadlines aloud, and how often your team reviews them across live deals.
fields.example: Ten-day inspection period with the seller refusing credits or a price cut, so written cancellation is set for day 9 [Larry Mastropieri — CSHBzTZo3Yc @ 00:00:45]. Every deadline is read aloud at an 8 a.m. operations call covering roughly 40 live deals. Contingencies clear just by missing the date, and once cleared, they stay cleared.

fields.name: state_deposit_rules
fields.prompt: Note the state-specific deposit rules that govern this contract. Record who must sign to release funds, whether a cancellation out of compliance sends the money to the seller, and any local deposit custom or liquidated damages trigger day.
fields.example: Connecticut deal: both the buyer's attorney and the seller's attorney must agree to release the funds, and the contract, not a handshake or verbal agreement, is what protects the deposit [Charles Nedder | Greenwich CT Real Estate — xyiyeiBkCqQ @ 00:03:07]. Greenwich custom calls for 10% at contract signing, $200,000 on a $2,000,000 home, wired to the buyer's attorney.

fields.name: wholesaler_emd_practice
fields.prompt: If you are wholesaling, state whether you will post earnest money at all, how much, and where it is held. Record how your end buyer's non-refundable deposit backs your exposure and the escrow release clause that routes it to you.
fields.example: Wholesale contract with a 10-day inspection period, purchased and sold the same day within minutes, with no earnest money deposit from the investor [LearnREInvesting — 1ZAn99Atwe8 @ 00:02:17]. Where a deposit is required, the end buyer's meaningful non-refundable deposit sits with escrow under a release clause, so their skin in the game covers the wholesaler's EMD [The Full Deal REI — H-3pmQVYvCI @ 00:06:18].

fields.name: fund_seasoning
fields.prompt: Record when the cash used for earnest money and closing landed in the bank account. Confirm it has seasoned long enough to be sourceable for the loan type, and note any low-down-payment program that returns the deposit at closing.
fields.example: Cash moved into the account 60 days before going under contract, because money deposited the day before the EMD wire is non-sourceable on conventional, FHA, USDA and Fannie- and Freddie-backed loans [The Treasure Valley Home Show — 5lKK7iczAKk @ 00:19:20]. On low-down programs the deposit can come back: CCM zero-down buyers got all of it, an Idaho Housing buyer all but $500.

fields.name: proof_of_funds_source
fields.prompt: Identify the proof-of-funds source attached to this offer: local hard money lender, transactional lender letter, paid letter service, or bank statement. Confirm the name matches the offer, the amount is exact, and the address is included.
fields.example: Letter pulled from a local hard money lender, which Brent Daniels finds more powerful than a national brand [Brent Daniels - Wholesaling Inc — AcL3tusr27o @ 00:05:33]. Backup: Tailwind letters at $1.99 each or $9.99 a month, generated from contract name, property address and price [FlipThisWholesaler — FOfp5iWKVkc @ 00:04:20]. The name on the letter matches the buyer named on the offer.

fields.name: agent_pof_pushback
fields.prompt: Plan your response if the listing agent rejects a soft proof of funds. State whether you will offer a short contingency, replace the agent, or downgrade to a financed offer, and note who you expect to demand hard proof.
fields.example: About 90% of agents accept a soft letter because it checks a box; the other 10% demand hard proof [Flipping Mastery TV — 9NXVYf_SZCA @ 00:03:34]. Jerry Norton offers a five-to-seven-day contingency, and says to find a new agent when one rejects the letter. Steph Davis instead downgrades, making the offer with a financing contingency.

fields.name: prorations_and_taxes
fields.prompt: Calculate the property tax and HOA prorations that change the cash due at closing. Record the daily proration math, any unpaid property taxes, hold-and-pay collections, and which generic seller credit lines you asked the lender to itemize.
fields.example: September closing in Oregon with no tax amount on the county lien, so title collects about 115% of last year's bill and refunds the overage [Julee Felsman | Workshop Team | Guaranteed Rate — faIlHE0Vtco @ 00:11:22]. The lender was asked to itemize the generic seller credits line, since a missing tax proration shifts the cash actually due at closing.

fields.name: wire_fraud_defense
fields.prompt: Write your wire fraud defense. Record the escrow phone number established early and independently, how every wire will be verified, the red flags that stop a transfer, and the exact recall steps if funds appear compromised.
fields.example: Every wire is verified by calling escrow on a number set early, never one printed in the email [Katherine Brough — h1TnczbK_bE @ 00:02:06]. Any request to wire to a new bank account stops the transfer. If compromised: call the bank immediately to recall, notify escrow and the agent, and report to FBI IC3 [Think Escrow! — f-7Rw_JAZOA @ 00:08:49].

worksheets.completion_gate: Gate passed only when every contingency deadline is calendared, the deposit sits with a neutral holder on a sourceable wire, the proof of funds matches the offer name and amount, prorations are itemized, and every wire has been phone-verified on an independently established number.

worksheets.title: Gator EMD Lending and the Transactional Desk
worksheets.purpose: Build a small-check lending operation that advances wholesaler earnest money deposits for flat chunks and funds same-day double closes. Every dollar is routed through escrow and protected by HUD position, signed releases, and written title commitments before any wire leaves your account.
instructions: Complete the earnest money fields first and the transactional desk fields second, because the release paperwork habits you set on small deposits carry over to full A-to-B purchase funding.
Write every price as a dollar figure on a sample deal, not only as a percentage, so you can see the exact chunk or fee you collect.
Confirm each title-related answer by email and then by phone with the escrow officer before you treat the field as complete.
Record borrower limits as hard numbers: completed deals required, maximum open deals per borrower, and the minimum hours left in the inspection period.
Revisit the pricing and capital partner fields after every ten funded deals, and adjust them only when your loss record and turnaround times support the change.

fields.name: emd_demand_signal
fields.prompt: Record the share of wholesalers you believe lack earnest money in your market, then explain how that gap shapes your Gator 1.0 offer, including the typical deposit size you expect to advance and the flat chunk you plan to charge per deal.
fields.example: Pace Morby estimates 85% of wholesalers lack EMD cash, the core demand behind Gator 1.0 [Pace Morby — iVg9EsSij2c @ 00:00:00]. Pace's average EMD deal put up about $1,000 to $3,000 and returned $1,500 to $3,000 [Pace Morby — iVg9EsSij2c @ 00:00:46]. My plan: advance $2,000 per deposit and charge a flat $1,500 chunk, never interest.

fields.name: hud_position_check
fields.prompt: Describe exactly how you will confirm your position on the HUD before releasing an earnest money advance, naming the contract clause that routes the deposit back to you and the follow-up channel you use with the title company.
fields.example: Pace lent $1,500 of earnest money on a deal paying the wholesaler $25,000 only on condition of being on the HUD, and earned $5,000 [Pace Morby — -9RSC5hpr9o @ 00:04:29]. Before wiring, email title to confirm the due-diligence end date, the seller release, and that EMD returns to the lender, then follow up by phone [Pace Morby — T5jtdYhM6tQ @ 00:07:01].

fields.name: seller_release_file
fields.prompt: List the release documents you require at contracting, noting whether the property sits in a mutual release state, how the seller waives consent up front, and where the pre-signed title company form will live inside the transaction file.
fields.example: Have the seller pre-sign the title company's EMD release form at contracting and leave it in the file with a sticky note, because title policy can demand signed authorization [Pace Morby — qbBAO0ozP-0 @ 00:14:54]. In Texas and Utah, mutual release states, Pace's contract has the seller waive that consent up front [Pace Morby — A3l3Dg0cJLk @ 00:03:40].

fields.name: inspection_window_rule
fields.prompt: State the minimum time you require remaining in the inspection period before you fund an earnest money deposit, plus the written understanding you need from title or escrow and the upfront fee that filters out bad deals.
fields.example: Abdiel Garcia Rodriguez funds only inside the inspection period with at least 48 hours remaining and a written understanding from title or escrow [Abdiel Garcia Rodriguez — min0RpX32uc @ 00:05:30]. Pace charges $200 to $1,000 upfront to protect the lender and filter out bad deals [Pace Morby — T5jtdYhM6tQ @ 00:05:26]. My rule: 48 hours minimum and $500 upfront.

fields.name: borrower_screen
fields.prompt: Write your borrower screening questions, including the completed-deal count that earns funding, the exposure cap per borrower, the reporting cadence you demand, and the context clues inside an EMD request that signal something is wrong with the deal.
fields.example: Ask how many deals the borrower has completed; 25 is the signal Pace flags as worth funding [Pace Morby — OBl7C-hFLY4 @ 00:07:13]. Cap exposure at one or two deals per borrower with weekly reports [Pace Morby — S9WonQBbHG8 @ 00:40:17]. A '90 days' timeline or a '1%' figure in the ask signals trouble [Ryan Schrope — wpikXXbAYnE @ 00:17:06].

fields.name: transactional_pricing
fields.prompt: Set your double-close pricing schedule, showing the base points you charge, any volume ladder for repeat wholesalers, the dollar fee on a sample purchase price, and how you split that fee with any capital partner funding the wire.
fields.example: Ryan Schrope prices a $500,000 purchase at 1.5%, or $7,500, split about $3,750 each with a capital partner, money typically out one to two hours [Ryan Schrope — wpikXXbAYnE @ 00:24:45]. OrotonEquities ladders 2 points standard, 1.75 at 3+ deals, 1.5 at 6+, and 1.25 at 9+ [OrotonEquities — vtoojcHUwHU @ 00:02:29].

fields.name: release_trigger
fields.prompt: Define the exact release trigger for your transactional wire, naming which signatures must be complete on both legs, where the end buyer's money must sit, and the written return commitment you require from the title company before funding.
fields.example: Release funds only when both A-B and B-C sides are signed and the end buyer's money already sits in escrow [Oakwood Lending — VxkBvKoeA38 @ 00:02:33]. Ryan Schrope gets it in writing, signed by the title company, that the money wires back immediately upon receipt, typically within 30 minutes [Ryan Schrope — N4o948Y1Q-U @ 00:08:38].

fields.name: underwriting_stance
fields.prompt: Choose your underwriting stance on transactional files, explaining whether you run none, acquisition only, or more, which documents a wholesaler must bring, and how long you allow your money to stay out before the file becomes a bridge.
fields.example: Clicks Geek says bring two purchase and sale agreements, connect them with the title company, and it gets done with no underwriting and no delays [Clicks Geek — cgY-PRTdUB4 @ 00:01:58]. Hard Money Mike puts transactional funding at one to two days and about a point to a point and a half, versus 30-to-60-day bridge loans [Hard Money Mike — i2EHd_tEf1w @ 00:03:54].

fields.name: emd_fee_and_paper
fields.prompt: Record your earnest money deposit funding fee as a percentage of the deposit, compare it to the market range, and list the mutual release paperwork you require between wholesaler and seller alongside the purchase agreement before wiring.
fields.example: Ryan Schrope charges 40% of the deposit, $2,000 on $5,000, against a 20 to 50% market range, on deposits of about 1% of price [Ryan Schrope — wpikXXbAYnE @ 00:12:02]. On EMD deals, require a mutual release agreement signed between wholesaler and seller alongside the purchase agreement [Fund My Real Estate Deal — yWKbp0xDuE8 @ 00:09:28].

fields.name: capital_partner_dry_run
fields.prompt: Outline how you will bring in a capital partner, including the title company fraud check, the written confirmation of the funding source, the dry run you schedule first, and how you protect cash flow while money is out.
fields.example: With capital partners, vet the title company for fraud, get written confirmation of the funding source, and run a dry run first [Ryan Schrope — 2a2qJD8P3gI @ 00:15:34]. Ryan Schrope reports $3.7M funded in 30 days for about $83K profit across 15 deals, roughly one deal every other day [Ryan Schrope — xdTSPoFABEY @ 00:00:30].

worksheets.completion_gate: Do not fund a first deal until all ten fields are filled, the seller release form and mutual release agreement templates are in your file, a title company has signed a written commitment to wire your money back immediately upon receipt, and the end buyer's money is confirmed sitting in escrow.

worksheets.title: Private Money Terms, Security Documents and Usury Limits
worksheets.purpose: Structure private and hard money loans so pricing matches borrower experience, terms outlast the project, and first-position security is recorded before the wire. Keep the all-in cost under your state usury cap, and make sure joint venture paperwork is signed by the right entity.
instructions: Fill in the lender bucket map before quoting any borrower, so every loan term lines up with the repayment clock of the capital behind it.
Price loans by experience tier and write the leverage, points, rate, and closing speed for each tier on one sheet.
Treat the security checklist and the closing instruction letter as non-negotiable gates, and leave the wire decision open until both are complete.
Run the all-in APR calculation on every new loan structure, counting points, origination, processing, appraisal, and lender-required surveys over the actual term.
Have an attorney review the note, security instrument, and any joint venture template, and confirm the signing entity is never you personally.

fields.name: lender_bucket_map
fields.prompt: Sort your current and target lenders into A, B, and C buckets, recording each lender's check size, expected payoff clock, and the exit you will use to clear them, so repayment timing never collides with your project calendar.
fields.example: Pace Morby says lenders at $25,000 or less want repayment within six months, while lenders at $100,000 to $300,000 rarely want it back within a year [Pace Morby — UtlUmrdNU8Y @ 00:00:52]. About 80% of Pace's lenders are C-bucket investors exiting within 3 months to 2 years [Pace Morby — UtlUmrdNU8Y @ 00:05:30].

fields.name: loan_pricing_sheet
fields.prompt: Write your loan pricing sheet by borrower experience tier, listing interest rate, points, leverage on purchase and rehab, and closing speed, then note which tier a first-time flipper lands in versus a borrower with several completed deals.
fields.example: SEP Capital charges 12% plus 3 points for experienced flippers and 4-6 points for everyone else [Hard Money Mastermind — 9ISIUnJvomU @ 00:16:20]. Gabrial Carter's High Roller program offers 90% of purchase, 100% of rehab, 1 point, about 10%, no appraisal, and a 24-48 hour close for 3-4+ deals and 680+ credit [Beyond The Deals Podcast — tbL4i7Pr1EM @ 00:17:56].

fields.name: lien_position_gate
fields.prompt: Document the security checklist that must clear before you wire private money, covering lien position, recording timing, title search, and lender's title insurance, and state the second-position loan requests you will refuse outright and exactly why.
fields.example: Wire only after a recorded mortgage or deed of trust, a title search, and lender's title insurance are in place; the lien must be recorded at or before closing [Venus Venture — qHujP7kjj4Y @ 00:01:38]. Invest Away refuses 20-25% second-position flip loans and is still waiting on early junior-lien money [Real Estate Explainer — 1UWrNExO1Ak @ 00:17:54].

fields.name: term_padding
fields.prompt: Enter the project timeline your borrower presents, then set the note term you will actually write, explaining how much cushion you add so a slipping schedule never forces a fire sale or an expensive extension at a higher rate.
fields.example: Ryan Dossey sets the note term at 12 months when the project plan says 3, so a slipping timeline never forces a fire sale [Ryan Dossey — UlOFHwYtg7E @ 00:05:09]. Toño Flores runs transactional money on a typical 30-day term with 60 days max, logging 48 deals and zero losses for the year [Toño Flores — fv1IoI6DQn8 @ 00:03:10].

fields.name: referral_engine
fields.prompt: Map your loan origination referral engine, naming the partner types you will approach, the share of origination fee you pay them, and the outreach routine you will run each week to reach realtors who control deal flow.
fields.example: SEP Capital pays referral partners about 15% of the origination fee even when they never asked, since referrals drive most of its business [Hard Money Mastermind — 9ISIUnJvomU @ 00:09:17]. Originator Lisa pulled business cards off brokerage walls, called every realtor, and landed a $1.5M St. Pete condo loan against an ARV near $2.6-2.7M [Hard Money Mastermind — 9ISIUnJvomU @ 00:19:07].

fields.name: document_stack
fields.prompt: List every document in your private loan file, pairing the promissory note with its recorded security instrument, and explain how you cross-reference their terms and why you avoid land contracts when you may later sell the note.
fields.example: Use a promissory note with a deed of trust or mortgage, and skip land contracts, which make notes harder to sell [Damen Capital Fund — mrt2bJ7XfNU @ 00:07:53]. The deed of trust is the security instrument that lets the lender foreclose [Investor Army — ltZrMvVSfdw @ 00:02:46]; cross-reference note and deed so terms stay consistent [Gary Pryde — nKwv-ImRqjo @ 00:05:13].

fields.name: closing_instruction_letter
fields.prompt: Describe the release conditions for your loan wire, including the settlement statement review, the signed closing instruction letter from title, and the signing methods you reject, given that the title company does not represent you as lender.
fields.example: Hard Money Mastermind never releases a wire until the HUD-1 is reviewed and title has signed the closing instruction letter, because the title company does not represent the lender, and it rejects powers of attorney and remote online notaries [Hard Money Mastermind — bNJYDcDSFxU @ 00:17:38]. Personal guarantees back 98% of its loans [Hard Money Mastermind — bNJYDcDSFxU @ 00:05:23].

fields.name: usury_apr_check
fields.prompt: Recalculate the all-in APR on a sample loan, adding points, origination, processing, appraisal, and lender-required surveys over the actual term, then compare the result against the usury cap for your state and borrower type before quoting.
fields.example: Scott Horne pegs Texas at 18% for individuals and 24% for corporate entities, counting points, origination, processing, appraisal, and lender-required surveys toward APR [Scott Horne's Owner Finance Network — XdrwPF-D1FI @ 00:00:32]. Lender Link fixes California at a 10% APR cap with points and fees included, so a 9.99% note rate is not automatically safe [Lender Link — W1fiiFnsFhE @ 00:01:20].

fields.name: modification_and_default
fields.prompt: Explain how you will handle a borrower who needs more time, separating a pure time extension from changes to rate, points, or new advances, and describe how default interest could compound if a refinance stalls on your loan.
fields.example: On California paper, never add rate, points, or new advances through an unlicensed modification; a pure time extension is the only safe change [Lender Link — W1fiiFnsFhE @ 00:06:32]. In one Ayala Law PA trial, a 21% default rate on a $5M loan pushed the balance to about $6.4M while refinancing was delayed [Ayala Law PA — 0cBnXayz9w4 @ 00:01:58].

fields.name: jv_agreement_plan
fields.prompt: Decide whether your EMD or gap-funding deals will run on a joint venture agreement, noting the entity that signs, the attorney budget for the template, and how you address the lawsuit risk critics attach to these agreements.
fields.example: Pace Morby says Gator EMD funding needs a JV agreement 100% of the time, budgeting roughly $12-13K for the attorney-drafted template [Pace Morby — 9-Vzu27aIq0 @ 00:01:20]. Toby Mathis warns never to sign it in your own name, since it could be treated as a general partnership [Toby Mathis Esq | Tax Planning & Asset Protection — FiBdpAVfzMo @ 00:03:13].

worksheets.completion_gate: The worksheet is complete when all ten fields are filled, a sample loan passes the usury check for its state and borrower type, the note and recorded deed of trust or mortgage are cross-referenced, title has signed the closing instruction letter, and the lien records at or before closing.

worksheets.title: Bridge Debt, Credit Lines and 0% Business Credit Stacks
worksheets.purpose: Use short-term bridge loans, lines of credit, and 0% business card stacks only when an exit is written first and leverage and costs are converted to dollars. Prepare the personal credit file and bank sequence in advance so approvals land in the higher limit tiers.
instructions: Write both bridge exits before requesting any quote, and match each exit to a slow or hot market.
Convert every fee, flat monthly charge, and rate into dollars on a sample draw or loan amount before comparing offers.
Audit your personal credit file and build bank relationships three to six months before a planned 0% stack.
Apply in the sequence you documented, and stop if any single bureau approaches three hard inquiries.
Revisit the runway and repayment fields monthly, and clear balances before any promotional window ends.

fields.name: bridge_exit_plan
fields.prompt: Write a primary exit and a backup exit for your bridge loan, matching each to slow or hot market conditions, and state the sale or refinance date that clears the debt inside the lender's term without a costly extension.
fields.example: Every bridge loan has an exit and the lender asks about it before almost anything else, so write a primary and second exit before applying [Michael Daniel Investments — 0EcBhBq5U08 @ 00:02:05]. Easy Lending USA warns against using bridge debt as long-term money; refinance or sell inside the 12-18 month term [Easy Lending USA — GcefOZxHIAg @ 00:05:18].

fields.name: leverage_tier
fields.prompt: Identify the leverage tier you qualify for on an investor bridge loan, listing your completed deal count, FICO score, expected loan-to-value, and whether the lender will size the loan off cost basis or appraised value given seasoning.
fields.example: Easy Lending USA tiers leverage at 75% for 2+ deals and FICO 620+, 72.5% for one deal, and 70% for new borrowers at FICO 650+ [Easy Lending USA — GcefOZxHIAg @ 00:03:53]. Keep every receipt on properties owned under 12 months, because the bridge sizes off cost basis until the asset is seasoned [Easy Lending USA — GcefOZxHIAg @ 00:04:35].

fields.name: bridge_quote_interrogation
fields.prompt: Record the answers from every bridge quote to four questions: what an extension costs, whether a prepayment penalty applies, how draws are staged, and what exit the lender expects, then flag any junk fees or Dutch interest found.
fields.example: Michael Daniel Investments asks what an extension costs, whether there is a prepayment penalty, how draws are staged, and what exit is expected [Michael Daniel Investments — 0EcBhBq5U08 @ 00:03:02]. Rene Nelson screens terms for Dutch interest and junk fees like $250-500 draw charges and surprise inspections [Rene Nelson — VIt86OFRY3Y @ 00:54:38].

fields.name: buy_before_sell_math
fields.prompt: If you are buying before selling, calculate your combined loan-to-value across both homes, the program fee in dollars, and the cheaper alternative you tested, such as a HELOC, recast, or sale contingency, before committing to bridge debt.
fields.example: SEI Mortgage caps the bridge at 75% combined loan-to-value across the current and new home [SEI Mortgage - Ryan Marks — d8gbJrywXFE @ 00:00:46]. Steve Ferguson's zero-interest program advances about 70% of departing-home value for 2.4% or $9,000, whichever is higher [The Mortgage Man - Steve Ferguson — AGFnuSOGL68 @ 00:03:38].

fields.name: rehab_reserves
fields.prompt: Budget unit turns and reserves for any bridge-financed value-add project, entering your per-unit turn cost, the reserve amount kept inside the deal, and the safeguard that stops reserves from ever being diverted into another property during the term.
fields.example: Rene Nelson budgets unit turns at $25K to $30K each, not the $5K to $10K sponsors assume [Rene Nelson — VIt86OFRY3Y @ 00:21:33]. Keep reserves inside the deal; diverted reserves forced a cross-collateralization [Rene Nelson — VIt86OFRY3Y @ 00:37:31]. Private bridge money runs 11% to 12%, with interest-only payments near 1% of balance monthly [Rene Nelson — VIt86OFRY3Y @ 00:43:19].

fields.name: line_of_credit_cost
fields.prompt: Compare the cost of a sample draw on a bank line of credit against an online lender's offer, converting any monthly flat fee into an approximate APR so you pay interest only on what you actually draw.
fields.example: Fast Business Lending prices a $20K draw from a $50K line over six months at about $583 from a bank versus $1,800 to $3,488 from online lenders, and a 1.55% monthly flat fee works out to roughly 31% APR [Fast Business Lending — -EPbq7NKBZY @ 00:02:17]. Interest applies only to the $20K drawn, not the full $50K limit.

fields.name: personal_file_readiness
fields.prompt: Audit your personal credit file before a 0% stack, recording your score, utilization, recent hard inquiries on each bureau, and comparable personal limits, then decide whether you are ready or need to wait before applying anywhere.
fields.example: Operators want a 680 minimum, 720-plus preferred, utilization near 10%, and comparable personal limits that set the business ceiling. Colin Matthew holds every bureau under three hard inquiries, because three on any single bureau means flat denial at most banks [Colin Matthew — WAqBw-d5K44 @ 00:01:42]. My file: 702 score, 12% utilization, one inquiry per bureau.

fields.name: bank_sequence
fields.prompt: Lay out your bank application sequence, naming which lender goes first and the reason it leads, how you will build relationship deposits before applying, and whether you ask each bank to place multiple cards on one hard pull.
fields.example: Chase goes first because it is the most inquiry-sensitive lender, and Colin Matthew stacks $70-100K at Chase after a seasoned checking deposit [Colin Matthew — WAqBw-d5K44 @ 00:02:27]. Naam Wynn measured $20K cold versus $150K-plus with a relationship [Naam Wynn — LktXzMB-Sis @ 00:05:04]. Navy Federal and PNC put multiple cards on one pull only if asked [Cal Barton — Eh5z4F-toEI @ 00:10:20].

fields.name: promo_runway
fields.prompt: For each card in your stack, record whether 0% covers purchases, balance transfers, or both, when the promotional clock starts, and how many months of runway remain, so you never fund a deal on a short treadmill.
fields.example: Confirm whether each card's 0% covers purchases, balance transfers, or both before moving a dollar [HowToCredit — 0jZD4_NoCTs @ 00:01:43]. Amex Blue Business Plus counts its 12-month window from account opening, while US Bank counts billing cycles [HowToCredit — 0jZD4_NoCTs @ 00:04:32]. Cal Barton calls anything under 9 months a treadmill [Cal Barton — Eh5z4F-toEI @ 00:09:05].

fields.name: stack_deployment_exit
fields.prompt: Describe how you will deploy stacked capital into a real estate or inventory play, including the liquidation cost, the amount you could repay within six months if the deal stalls, and the exit that clears balances before promotions end.
fields.example: Marvin Francois borrows only what could be repaid within six months if the deal stalls [Marvin Francois — 6xdE38E2F8Q @ 00:04:43]. Gap Funding writes the exit first: sale, refinance, or a set repayment date before the promo ends [Gap Funding | 100% Real Estate Financing — ItOMPgJwT_4 @ 00:05:21]. Liquidation runs 2.5% to about 6% depending on the route.

worksheets.completion_gate: Do not sign bridge debt or open a stack until all ten fields are complete, a primary and second exit are written with dates, every card's 0% coverage and start date are confirmed, and the amount borrowed could be repaid within six months if the deal stalls.
